chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Salim and ʿAli ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who died during travel, and there were no women with her, nor any mahram. He said: “The places of wudu (ablution) are washed from her, salat (prayer) is performed over her, and she is buried.”

key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman, the deceased female in this legal case
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male unmarriageable kin, whose presence affects burial handling rulings
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel, indicating the circumstance of hardship or absence of normal means
key_terms.مَوْضِعُ الْوُضُوءِ: the bodily areas washed in wudu (ablution), to be washed here instead of full ghusl
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا: the funeral salat (prayer) is performed over her

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a woman dies while traveling and no women or mahram are present to wash her body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the case of a woman who dies while traveling without any women or mahram present to perform the full ghusl. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that only the parts of wudu (ablution) be washed, then the funeral salat (prayer) be offered over her and she be buried. It addresses ritual purity and burial procedure under necessity.
